findings.summary: gate_yield.py cmd_rollup registered the per_gate key BEFORE inspecting the event name, so ANY non-gate producer riding the one write path minted a phantom zero-yield gate row in the retirement instrument — the integration-adversary PROVED IT BY EXECUTION at plan re-review (three usage events -> `| readable-surface | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |`, then `candidates` reported the non-gate in its measured denominator) and both adversaries independently converged on the same seam. Fixed at the owner: the ROSTER decision (closed GATE_EVENTS vocabulary) is now separate from the COUNTING decision, for every future producer; usage events route to their own table; unknown events stay ignored-without-a-row.

The approved plan's first D5 design classified host from the bin's __file__ path / an installer marker and suppressed logging when unrecognised. This repo has no .claude/bin/ and no marker — it dogfoods via the marketplace plugin — so BOTH real invocation paths classified as not-Claude and the experiment would have produced a permanently empty usage record, auto-reading as `kill` on 2026-09-30 regardless of use. Replaced at the producer: _common.log_yield_event stamps host from host-runtime-provided signals (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR / TDD_PLAYBOOK_PROJECT_ROOT), unknown is LABELLED and still logged, never suppressed — all three directions pinned explicitly (an inherited session env would pass at home and fail in CI).

test_agents.py's opus-pin check iterated a hand list with no completeness guard, so the four new judgment agents would have shipped with `model: opus` NEVER CHECKED, green. Guard added BEFORE the agents: PINNED|INHERIT must equal the real directory, vacuity-guarded, with a planted unclassified-agent detector.

The first full gate run went RED at the calibration stage: five new gate surfaces (4 briefs + /readable) had no covering ledger entries — the gate-surface ledger working as designed. Entries registered with expect=up for the four briefs (each born with its plant/control pair, so the first live run scores recall and FP from zero) and expect=none for the narration command. An auto-checkpoint landed the surfaces before the ledger commit; per the recovered 2026-08-07 precedent this is in-window late registration against the true baseline (3fafc9e), stated in the commit message rather than smoothed over.
findings.disposition: Ledger entries L-20260812-01..05 committed separately (e15bd84); ledger check exits 0 vs v1.33.1; the same-commit blind spot remains dated debt on gate-surface-ledger.

findings.summary: Twice during release verification the operator (the model) piped a checker into grep/head and echoed $? — reading the FILTER's exit code as the checker's, exactly the §4a discarded-truth sin this repo's gate script warns about. Both self-caught on re-run (the scoreboard planted probe first reported a false rc, and the as-of expiry proof reported rc=0 from head); both re-verified unpiped before any claim was recorded. Named here because a verification habit that survives two occurrences in one release is a candidate for the next planted-error probe.
findings.disposition: All recorded claims re-verified with unpiped rc. The exitcode_guard exists for exactly this and ships opt-in; whether to opt it in for this repo is David's call, noted not smuggled.

findings.summary: The four agents pass --dry-run validation and R1 coverage but NO live run has executed their plant/control pairs (the 2026-08-06 run largely env-failed, unresolved: ~20 INVALID rows, one BLOCKING FAIL on red-first-verifier's control). Tagging v1.34.0 before a live calibration would ship uncalibrated verifiers with a green dry-run reading as evidence. Precondition registered as dated debt (role-adversaries-live-calibration, expires 2026-08-31) with the decision point stated: tag-without-the-agents / wait / drop, made deliberately.
